rationale: Start with a broad scouting gradient to locate the elution window and critical pairs while minimizing the risk of missing strongly retained compounds. The moderate temperature leaves room to explore temperature-dependent selectivity in either direction.

Change temperature while holding the gradient fixed to test selectivity in the closely spaced central cluster. The current last peak is comfortably below 10 minutes, so resolving the critical pairs is the priority.
Use a shallower gradient at the better temperature to improve separation of the remaining critical pair. The 6.58-minute last peak leaves substantial room to gain resolution without a time penalty.

An intermediate gradient duration should balance the two competing critical pairs: the pair at R 1.00 improved with a longer gradient, while the pair now at R 1.47 slightly worsened. This may bring both above 1.5 while keeping the last peak below 10 minutes.
The maximum CRF is already achieved; retain injection 4 as the benchmark. Raise temperature one step to seek earlier elution while testing whether both critical pairs remain fully resolved.

Return to 55 C, since 60 C nearly merged a critical pair. Increase the starting organic fraction one step to seek a shorter fully resolved separation, retaining injection 4 as the maximum-score benchmark.

Slightly reduce the gradient slope to recover the R 1.29 pair while preserving the improved separation of the other critical pair. This narrower organic window may achieve full resolution with a last peak slightly earlier than injection 4.

With a maximum-score method secured, test the opposite temperature extreme for a faster selectivity window. Cooling may separate the central cluster in a different order; the broad gradient limits the risk of excessive retention.

Test a substantially steeper gradient at 60 C to see whether the nearly coeluting pair crosses into a resolved reversed order. This explores a much faster separation while retaining injection 4 as the proven maximum-score method.

Test whether a higher starting organic fraction at 60 C separates the critical pair on the reversed-order side without the compression caused by the six-minute gradient. This also seeks earlier elution than the established fully resolved method.

Lower the starting organic fraction one step to recover separation of the early pair and measure how the two central critical pairs respond. This tests whether the fast 60 C region can support full resolution without compressing the first peaks.

Test whether a steeper gradient at 40 C opens a different selectivity window in the central cluster. The maximum-score method is already secured, so this injection explores a substantially faster alternative rather than accepting marginal resolution at 60 C.

Refine the near-perfect result from injection 7 by lowering the endpoint one more step. The slightly shallower gradient should lift the R 1.47 pair above 1.5 while keeping the other critical pair resolved and the last peak below 10 minutes.

Test a higher starting organic fraction with a modest temperature reduction to seek a faster fully resolved window. Cooling should help retain the early peaks and shift central-pair selectivity, while injection 4 remains the best established method.

Return to the successful 55 C selectivity window and combine a higher starting organic fraction with a shallower gradient. This tests whether full resolution can be retained while advancing elution relative to the lower-starting-organic methods.

Reduce the slope from injection 15 to improve its sole unresolved pair, using the R 1.76 margin of the other critical pair. The last peak should remain below 10 minutes, potentially establishing another fully resolved method around the successful 55 C window.

Lower the endpoint one grid step from injection 16 to bring its R 1.41 pair above the full-credit threshold. The other critical pair has some resolution margin, and the last peak should still elute before the time penalty begins.

Preserve injection 4’s successful gradient slope but end the programmed ramp four minutes earlier. Because its last peak eluted before this new ramp ends at the outlet, this should retain full resolution and maximum CRF with a shorter programmed gradient.

Shorten the ramp another step while preserving the successful slope through the central critical cluster. The final hold will test whether the last compound can still elute within 10 minutes, retaining maximum CRF with a shorter programmed gradient.

Test a slope between injections 7 and 13, where the limiting pair crossed the full-resolution threshold. This should shorten the fully resolved separation from injection 13 while retaining more margin for the other critical pair than injection 4.

Test a slightly shallower slope than injection 13 to increase the limiting-pair margin while checking that the competing pair stays above 1.5. This refines the robustness of the maximum-score region; injection 4 remains the fastest proven fully resolved method.

Test a small slope increase from the fastest fully resolved method, rather than the larger increase in injection 2. This brackets the speed limit of the successful 55 C window while retaining injection 4 as the maximum-score fallback.

Back off from the steeper slope that lost resolution and preserve injection 13’s fully resolved slope in an eight-minute ramp. Its last peak should elute before the new gradient endpoint reaches the outlet, retaining maximum CRF with a shorter programmed gradient.

Shorten injection 17’s programmed ramp by two minutes while keeping a slightly shallower slope to protect its limiting pair. This should preserve full resolution and elution before 10 minutes; injection 4 remains the fastest proven maximum-score method.

Finish with an untested endpoint-duration combination that preserves the fastest proven fully resolved gradient slope. All peaks should elute before the endpoint affects the chromatogram, retaining CRF 1.000 and the approximately 7.60-minute last peak of injection 4.
